title: the known planes of existence

banner.title: Appendix 1: the known planes of existence - the D&DG walk round nineteen, print pp. 128-133: the inner planes (the Prime Material, Positive, Negative, four Elemental, four Para-Elemental), the Ethereal, Shadow and Astral planes, the seventeen Outer Planes with their alignment bands, the ethereal and astral travel-and-combat rules, the Ether Cyclone and the psychic wind, the silver-cord doctrine, the two encounter tables (31 and 24 rows), the two random plane-determination tables, and the character subtable level bands. FIG. 4 and FIG. 5 of print p. 131 remain the open pixel-work box.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the extract/ddg tesseract pass (pNNN_full.txt + pNNN_tsv.tsv, print = pdf - 1, pages 129-134; the second printing) with the tsv x-y geometry as the fold-swap, dropped-glyph and band arbiter - the psm-4 fold garbled the psychic wind 13-16 row (Blocwozr;tfefr;:ourse), the inner random-table bands (8.9, 1011, the N of N-hegative) and the BARDT footnote glyph, all adjudicated by geometry plus the collation voice; the collation voice: the 1eonline L&L x1.htm appendix transcription. The adjudications: the ethereal elemental-earth ] glyph = 1 (the w6 token at the numbers column x-position), the astral Titan lesser 93-97 pinned by the print over the L&L 92-97 typo, the astral-only numbers read from the L&L voice (the tesseract dropped the single-number tokens), the Tifan, major garble = Titan, major, the inner random Negative band 5-7 adjudicated by band arithmetic (the 1-20 tiling), and the character subtable bard footnote (the BARDT print cell is the footnote glyph, the 91h is 9th).

audit_comment: APPENDIX 1: THE KNOWN PLANES OF EXISTENCE - the D&DG walk round nineteen, print pp. 128-133: the inner planes, the ethereal and astral travel-and-combat rules, the seventeen Outer Planes, the two encounter tables, the Ether Cyclone, the psychic wind, the silver-cord doctrine and the character subtable level bands; FIG. 4/5 remain the open pixel-work box.

tables.name: the ethereal encounter grid
col_comments: The shared creature-roster ordinals (39 labels; the astral-only demons, devils, night hag and rakshasa follow the ethereal roster; the labels ride the data file)
The percentile band lows (01-04 aerial servant through 98-00 xorn)
The percentile band highs (the printed 00 = 100, the R863 encounter-grid convention)
The numbers-encountered lows (0 = the human traveller character-subtable row)
The numbers-encountered highs (the ethereal elemental, earth ] print garble adjudicated 1 by the geometry and the L&L voice)
The flag cells (1 = the asterisked perceptions-extend creatures - basilisk, cockatrice, gorgon, medusa; 2 = the human traveller character subtable row)

tables.name: the astral encounter grid
col_comments: The shared creature-roster ordinals (the demons 31-33, the devils 34-36, the night hag 37 and the rakshasa 38 are the astral-only entries)
The percentile band lows (01-04 aerial servant through 98-00 titan major)
The percentile band highs (the printed 00 = 100)
The numbers-encountered lows (0 = the human traveller character-subtable row)
The numbers-encountered highs (the single-number rows read 1 by the L&L voice - the tesseract dropped the tokens; TITAN LESSER 93-97 pinned by the print over the L&L 92-97 typo)
The flag cells (1 = the asterisked creatures; 2 = the human traveller character subtable row)

tables.name: the outer planes grid
col_comments: The print list positions 1-17 (Seven Heavens through Concordant Opposition, the print p. 129 order)
The layers-word flags (Elysium, Olympus, Gladsheim, Limbo, Pandemonium, the Abyss, Tarterus, Acheron)
The descriptor cells (0 none, 1 the 666 layers of the Abyss, 2 the Three Glooms of Hades, 3 the furnaces of Gehenna, 4 the nether layers of Acheron)

tables.name: the cyclone grid
col_comments: The cyclone dice band lows (1-10, 11-15, 16-18, 19-20)
The cyclone dice band highs

The cyclone effect codes (1 random direction at 120 per round plus 1 check, 2 blown to a different plane plus the usual checks, 3 lost 5-60 days then a different plane, 4 lost 10-120 days plus the save-versus-spells-or-Astral rule)

tables.name: the wind grid
col_comments: The wind dice band lows (1-12, 13-16, 17-19, 20)
The wind dice band highs

The wind effect codes (1 slowed plus 1 check, 2 blown off course and lost 2-20 days then return, 3 a different destination, 4 the save-versus-magic silver-cord rule and lost 4-40 days; the 13-16 Blocwozr;tfefr;:ourse print garble adjudicated blows-off-course by the L&L voice)

tables.name: the inner random grid
col_comments: The inner random d20 band lows (the 8.9 and 1011 fold garbles adjudicated 8-9 and 10-11; the Negative row band 5-7 adjudicated by band arithmetic - the printed band glyph garbled to the N of N-hegative)
The inner random d20 band highs
The inner plane codes (0 Prime Material, 1 alternate world, 2 Positive, 3 Negative, 4 Earth, 5 Fire, 6 Water, 7 Dust, 8 Heat, 9 Ice, 10 Vapor, 11 Ethereal, 12 Shadow)

tables.name: the outer random grid
col_comments: The outer random d20 band lows (Astral 1-3 through Concordant Opposition 20)
The outer random d20 band highs

The outer plane codes (0 Astral, 1 Seven Heavens, 2 Twin Paradises, 3 Elysium, 4 Happy Hunting Grounds, 5 Olympus, 6 Gladsheim, 7 Limbo, 8 Pandemonium, 9 Abyss, 10 Tarterus, 11 Hades, 12 Gehenna, 13 Nine Hells, 14 Acheron, 15 Nirvana, 16 Arcadia, 17 Concordant Opposition)

tables.name: the para-elemental grid
col_comments: The para-elemental ordinals (0 Ice, 1 Dust, 2 Heat, 3 Vapor - the print p. 128 list order)
The first elemental codes (0 Air, 1 Earth, 2 Fire, 3 Water - the print list order)
The second elemental codes (Ice where Air and Water meet, Dust at the conjunction of Air and Fire, Heat where Fire and Earth converge - lava, Vapor at the meeting of Earth and Water)

consts.name: plnWindPct

bools.name: plnPluralUniverses
bools.comment: there exists an infinite number of parallel universes and planes of existence in the fantastic multiverse of ADVANCED DUNGEONS AND DRAGONS

bools.name: plnOnlyNormalTied
bools.comment: the charts and explanations show only the various planes tied to that of normal existence

bools.name: plnParallelsNotShown
bools.comment: the parallel universes are not shown, and their existence might or might not be actual

bools.name: plnRealityRefereeDependent
bools.comment: all of these worlds co-exist, but how real each is depends entirely on the development of each campaign referee

bools.name: plnPmpCenter
bools.comment: the Prime Material Plane (or Physical Plane) is at the center of the Inner Planes

bools.name: plnPmpHousesUniverse
bools.comment: it houses the universe and all of its parallels

bools.name: plnPmpPlaneOfTerra
bools.comment: it is the plane of Terra, and your campaign, in all likelihood

bools.name: plnPmpBoundedByInner
bools.comment: the Prime Material is bounded or permeated by all of the Inner Planes and the Astral Plane

bools.name: plnPmpFourElements
bools.comment: the Prime Material Plane is made up of the four elements plus positive and negative energy

bools.name: plnPosEnergyLight
bools.comment: the Positive Material Plane is a place of energy and light, the source of much that is vital and active, the power supply for good

bools.name: plnPosConsumePrime
bools.comment: any creature from the Prime Material that tried to enter the Positive Material Plane (e.g. from the Ethereal Plane) would probably be instantly consumed by the powerful energies there

bools.name: plnNegAntiMatter
bools.comment: the Negative Material Plane is a place of anti-matter and negative force, the source of power for undead, the energy area from which evil grows

bools.name: plnNegUncertainCreatures
bools.comment: no one is certain what types of creature may exist on the Negative (or Positive) Material Plane

bools.name: plnNegDrainPrime
bools.comment: any creature from the Prime Material Plane would probably be completely drained of all life and energy

bools.name: plnEleSurroundPmp
bools.comment: the planes of Air, Earth, Fire and Water surround the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: plnEleInfiniteEffect
bools.comment: there are an infinite number of parallel Prime Material Planes, each bounded by the Elemental Planes, so the Elemental Planes are themselves infinite, in effect

bools.name: plnEleApparentSizes
bools.comment: do not be fooled by the apparent sizes of the planes represented in Fig. 1

bools.name: plnEleMoveViaPara
bools.comment: it is possible to actually physically move from one Elemental Plane to another by moving through the Para-Elemental Planes

bools.name: plnEleHomesOfCreatures
bools.comment: the Elemental Planes are the homes of many different kinds of elemental creatures, and some of them have the ability to travel to the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: plnEleTrafficHeaviest
bools.comment: there is probably more traffic between the Prime Material and the Elemental planes than between any others

bools.name: plnEleTravelGatesOrEthereal
bools.comment: the elemental traffic is usually either direct travel (through gates or summoning) or by way of the Ethereal Plane

bools.name: plnNexialDeepestOcean
bools.comment: nexial points in distant out-of-the-way places lead directly to the Elemental Planes: the deepest ocean leads to the Plane of Water

bools.name: plnNexialHighAtmosphere
bools.comment: high in the atmosphere leads to the Plane of Air

bools.name: plnNexialFarUnderground
bools.comment: far underground leads to the Plane of Earth

bools.name: plnNexialActiveVolcano
bools.comment: in an active volcano leads to the Plane of Fire

bools.name: plnNexialTemporary
bools.comment: temporary nexial points may also be established occasionally, such as an opening to the Elemental Plane of Fire in the middle of a raging forest fire

bools.name: plnParaAtConjunctions
bools.comment: where the Elemental Planes meet are the lesser Para-Elemental Planes

bools.name: plnParaHomes
bools.comment: these planes are home to many para-elementals, and they can be reached in the same manners the Elemental Planes can be reached

bools.name: plnEthSurroundsAll
bools.comment: the Ethereal Plane surrounds, touches and permeates all of the Inner Planes and the endless parallel worlds of the universe without being a part of them

bools.name: plnEthInsubstantial
bools.comment: the Ethereal Plane is basically insubstantial, and few real creatures actually live there

bools.name: plnEthFloatingIslands
bools.comment: there are rumors of floating islands of solid ether, populated by exiles, which drift about the Ethereal Plane

bools.name: plnEthPhantoms
bools.comment: to creatures on the Ethereal Plane, objects on the Prime Material Plane (or any of the Inner Planes) appear as incorporeal phantoms

bools.name: plnEthPassNoDifficulty
bools.comment: ethereal creatures may pass through these phantoms with no difficulty

bools.name: plnEthChillSpine
bools.comment: a person being passed through might experience a chill down the spine

bools.name: plnEthRealToEachOther
bools.comment: ethereal beings or things are real to each other

bools.name: plnEthNotToOuter
bools.comment: the Ethereal Plane does not extend to the Outer Planes, so it is not possible for creatures on those planes to go ethereal

bools.name: plnShadCoExists
bools.comment: the Plane of Shadow co-exists with the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: plnShadInteraction
bools.comment: it is a result of the interaction of that plane and the Positive and Negative Material Planes

bools.name: plnShadNegDarkPosLight
bools.comment: the Negative plane provides the darkness, and the Positive plane the light; these meet at the Prime Material Plane, which casts the shadow

bools.name: plnShadMutableCreatures
bools.comment: the Plane of Shadow is a place of distorted and mutable shadow-creatures, of white, black and all shades of gray

bools.name: plnAstRadiatesNonSpace
bools.comment: the Astral Plane radiates from the Prime Material to a non-space where endless vortices spiral to the parallel Prime Material Planes, and to the Outer Planes as well

bools.name: plnAstTravelUses
bools.comment: this plane can be used to travel to distant worlds, to parallel planes, or to the Outer Planes themselves

bools.name: plnAstTouchesUpperOnly
bools.comment: the Astral Plane touches only the upper layer of each of the Outer Planes, and of the Inner Planes it touches only the Prime Material (see Fig. 3)

bools.name: plnFig1Inner
bools.comment: FIG. 1 THE INNER PLANES: the Positive Material above, the Prime Material Plane at center within the Elemental band, the Negative Material below, the Ethereal Plane outermost

bools.name: plnFig2Elemental
bools.comment: FIG. 2 THE ELEMENTAL PLANES: one way of visualizing the Elemental Planes relationship to each other

bools.name: plnFig3Outer
bools.comment: FIG. 3 THE OUTER PLANES: the Outer Planes contacting each other at their topmost layers, the Astral Plane between them and the Inner Planes

bools.name: plnFig45PixelWork
bools.comment: FIG. 4 and FIG. 5 (print p. 131) - the character alignment graph and the planes-of-alignment figures, the open pixel-work box of the gap report, not pinned in this round

bools.name: plnOutHomesOfDeities
bools.comment: the Outer Planes are the homes of the deities and the source of alignment (religious/philosophical/ethical ideals)

bools.name: plnOutExactCorrespondence
bools.comment: there is an exact correspondence between alignment and the Outer Planes; the alignment positions on the Character Alignment Graph match up exactly with the Outer Planes of identical alignment

bools.name: plnOutDegreeNotAbsolute
bools.comment: alignment is a matter of degree rather than absolute definition

bools.name: plnOutLeTendsGehenna
bools.comment: a lawful evil character who tended towards neutral evil would probably end up in Gehenna rather than Hades or the Nine Hells

bools.name: plnOutContactTopmost
bools.comment: the seventeen Outer Planes contact each other at their topmost layers

bools.name: plnOutAdjacentMoves
bools.comment: it is possible to move directly from the upper layer of one Outer Plane to an adjacent one (though it is not necessarily advisable or safe)

bools.name: plnOutAbyssMoves
bools.comment: a being could go from the topmost layer of the Abyss to Pandemonium or Tarterus

bools.name: plnOutHadesMoves
bools.comment: it is likewise possible to move from Hades to Tarterus, Gehenna, or the plane of Concordant Opposition

bools.name: plnSevenHeavensAbsLG
bools.comment: the Seven Heavens of absolute lawful good

bools.name: plnTwinParadisesLNG
bools.comment: the Twin Paradises of lawful/neutral good

bools.name: plnElysiumLayersNG
bools.comment: the layers of Elysium of neutral good

bools.name: plnHappyHuntingCGNG
bools.comment: the Happy Hunting Grounds of chaotic/neutral good

bools.name: plnOlympusLayersACG
bools.comment: the layers of Olympus of absolute chaotic good

bools.name: plnGladsheimLayersNGC
bools.comment: the layers of Gladsheim (Asgard, Vanaheim, etc.) of neutral/good chaotics

bools.name: plnLimboLayersChaos
bools.comment: the layers of Limbo of neutral (absolute) chaos

bools.name: plnPandemoniumLayersNEC
bools.comment: the layers of Pandemonium of neutral/evil chaotics

bools.name: plnAbyssAbsCE
bools.comment: the 666 layers of the Abyss of absolute chaotic evil

bools.name: plnTarterusLayersNCE
bools.comment: the layers of Tarterus of neutral/chaotic evil

bools.name: plnHadesThreeGlooms
bools.comment: Hades' Three Glooms of neutral (absolute) evil

bools.name: plnGehennaFurnacesNLE
bools.comment: the furnaces of Gehenna of neutral/lawful evil

bools.name: plnNineHellsAbsLE
bools.comment: the Nine Hells of absolute lawful evil

bools.name: plnAcheronNetherNEL
bools.comment: the nether layers of Acheron of neutral/evil law

bools.name: plnNirvanaAbsLaw
bools.comment: Nirvana of neutral (absolute) law

bools.name: plnArcadiaNGL
bools.comment: the plane of Arcadia of neutral/good law

bools.name: plnConcordantOfOpposition
bools.comment: the plane of Concordant Opposition of true neutrals

bools.name: plnEthStateByMeans
bools.comment: a character can achieve the ethereal state by magic spells, magic items, magical ointment (oil of etherealness) or psionic discipline

bools.name: plnEthMoveInnerPlanes
bools.comment: it is possible to move to or about any of the Inner Planes which the Ethereal Plane permeates

bools.name: plnEthPlaneToPlane
bools.comment: it is possible to move from plane to plane ethereally

bools.name: plnEthWillMovement
bools.comment: to move on the Ethereal Plane, an entity has but to will movement for it to happen

bools.name: plnEthConcentrationHalts
bools.comment: if concentration upon movement lapses, progress immediately halts

bools.name: plnEthTirelessRapid
bools.comment: ethereal travel is tireless and rapid

bools.name: plnEthNoNeeds
bools.comment: creatures in ethereal state need neither food, drink, rest nor sleep

bools.name: plnEthShadowToShadow
bools.comment: ethereal creatures may move from plane to plane by moving from the shadow of one plane to the shadow of another, accomplished by concentrating upon moving to the desired destination

bools.name: plnEthMentalTrail
bools.comment: this gets easier with practice, as the being marks out a mental trail through the ether

bools.name: plnEncUnfamiliarTriple
bools.comment: if the party is following an unfamiliar path, check for encounters three times total: at the beginning, midpoint, and at the end of the journey

bools.name: plnEncEvasionFaster
bools.comment: evasion is possible only if the adventurers are able to move more quickly than the monster encountered

bools.name: plnEncEvasionFamiliar
bools.comment: evasion will occur only if the party is both following a familiar path

bools.name: plnEncEvasionIntelligence
bools.comment: and the least-intelligent member of the party has a higher intelligence score than the most-intelligent pursuer

bools.name: plnEncMentalFunction
bools.comment: due to the fact that ethereal travel is a function of mental concentration

bools.name: plnCycInnerFluctuations
bools.comment: the twisting vortex of the Ether Cyclone is caused by fluctuations of the Inner Planes

bools.name: plnCycOnlyBetweenPlanes
bools.comment: the cyclone is only encountered on ethereal journeys between planes

bools.name: plnCycSlowAddCheck
bools.comment: if travelling is involved, the party is slowed so as to incur 1 additional encounter check

bools.name: plnCycDifferentPlane
bools.comment: the cyclone blows to a plane different than that which the party is near or desires to travel to; the usual encounter checks must be made

bools.name: plnCycSaveSpells
bools.comment: unless a saving throw versus spells is made, the party is blown to the Astral Plane; if a save is successful, the party will still arrive at a randomly determined plane touched by the ether

bools.name: plnEthCombatReal
bools.comment: creatures on the Ethereal Plane are real to each other, and normal melee or spell casting is possible between ethereal beings

bools.name: plnEthCombatPartial
bools.comment: it is also possible to combat creatures who exist or function partially on the Ethereal Plane

bools.name: plnEthSpellsToPmp
bools.comment: it is only in these instances that spells can be cast from the Ethereal to the Prime Material Plane, and then they will only affect the creature with ethereal connections

bools.name: plnEthDamageActual
bools.comment: ethereal combat damage is actual damage

bools.name: plnAstPerceptionNote
bools.comment: the asterisked table creatures perceptions extend into the Astral and Ethereal Planes (as do their magical attack forms), but they do not actually travel therein; their possible appearance applies only when the encountering party is near to the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: plnAstBySpellsPsionics
bools.comment: astral travel is possible by various means including magic spells and psionic discipline

bools.name: plnAstTouchesSeventeen
bools.comment: the Astral Plane touches only the endless Prime Material Plane and the 17 first layers of the Outer Planes

bools.name: plnAstNoInnerOther
bools.comment: the Astral Plane does not touch any of the Inner Planes other than the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: plnAstClericalSpellRef
bools.comment: it is possible to move about, in, or to any of the Prime Material universes or to the first layers of the Outer Planes by means of astral travel (see the clerical astral spell for pertinent details)

bools.name: plnAstSpeedy
bools.comment: movement through the Astral Plane is speedy

bools.name: plnAstNoNeeds
bools.comment: while there the individual needs no food, drink, rest or even sleep

bools.name: plnAstConcentrateMove
bools.comment: beings in an astral state move from place to place simply by concentrating upon moving to the desired destination

bools.name: plnAstLearnsTheWay
bools.comment: as with ethereal travel, this gets easier with practice, as the astral traveller learns the way

bools.name: plnAstEvasionAsEthereal
bools.comment: astral evasion is handled as described under Ethereal Encounters

bools.name: plnWindUnknown
bools.comment: no one knows how or why the psychic wind blows, but all fear its effects

bools.name: plnWindSlow
bools.comment: the wind slows travel only, incurring 1 additional check for random encounter

bools.name: plnWindLostShort
bools.comment: the wind blows off course, and the party is lost for 2-20 days time, then must return to the starting place

bools.name: plnWindDifferentDest
bools.comment: the wind blows off course so that the party arrives at a different destination as determined by random method

bools.name: plnWindSaveMagic
bools.comment: the storm blows, and unless a saving throw versus magic is made, the silver cord is broken, and the party is killed

bools.name: plnWindLostLong
bools.comment: if a save is successful, the party is lost for 4-40 days and must return to the starting place thereafter

bools.name: plnWindNoCord
bools.comment: if astral projection does not involve a silver cord attachment, then the party concerned is both lost and arrives at a different destination when struck by a psychic storm wind

bools.name: plnAstCombatReal
bools.comment: astral beings are real to each other, and can cast spells and melee normally

bools.name: plnAstNoPossessions
bools.comment: astral travellers employing an astral spell or the psionic astral projection discipline do not carry their possessions with them into the Astral Plane (except for certain magic items that have a multi-planar existence, e.g. an amulet of the planes)

bools.name: plnAstNaturalWeaponry
bools.comment: beings travelling astrally by these modes will therefore have to rely on their natural weaponry or spells without material components in any astral melee

bools.name: plnAstDestroyBodyMost
bools.comment: most creatures can do no more than destroy the astral body, causing the silver cord to return to the material body and preventing further astral travel for a period of time

bools.name: plnAstPowerfulSnap
bools.comment: very powerful beings (gods, demigods, etc.) might be able to snap the silver cord, thus killing the astral and material bodies simultaneously

bools.name: plnInnerViaEthereal
bools.comment: travel among the Inner Planes is usually done by means of the Ethereal Plane, as it permeates all of the Inner Planes

bools.name: plnOuterCantGoEthereal
bools.comment: it is not possible for creatures on the Outer Planes to go ethereal

bools.name: plnGatesAvoidEthereal
bools.comment: as with all planar travel, it is also possible to pass directly from one plane to another by means of gates, thereby avoiding ethereal travel

bools.name: plnGateBySpell
bools.comment: a gate may be formed by a magic spell (such as a gate spell, or conjure elemental, which forms a direct opening between the planes)

bools.name: plnGateByItems
bools.comment: or a magic item (e.g. an amulet of the planes, a well of many worlds, a cubic gate, or any of the various elemental-summoning devices)

bools.name: plnGateByDivine
bools.comment: or divine intervention

bools.name: plnNexialDirect
bools.comment: there are also direct nexial points connecting the Prime Material and Elemental Planes

bools.name: plnOuterViaGatesOrAstral
bools.comment: travel to and from the Outer Planes is usually by means of gates or via the Astral Plane

bools.name: plnAstralEntryOnly
bools.comment: the Astral Plane can only be entered from the Prime Material Plane or one of the first layers of the 17 Outer Planes

bools.name: plnGatedComplete
bools.comment: if a being is gated to one of the Outer Planes, he comes complete with body and possessions, leaving no part of himself behind

bools.name: plnProjectionLeavesBody
bools.comment: if a being astrally projects and travels the Astral Plane to one of the Outer Planes, he leaves his material body behind on the Prime Material Plane, connected to his essence by a silver cord

bools.name: plnSilverCordKilled
bools.comment: if his material body is destroyed or the silver cord is snapped while he is in the Astral Plane, the being is permanently and irrevocably killed

bools.name: plnOuterBodyForms
bools.comment: if he moves to one of the Outer Planes from the Astral Plane, a body forms around him, but it is devoid of possessions

bools.name: plnBothBodiesCorded
bools.comment: both bodies are now connected by the silver cord, and if either body is destroyed, the being will continue on in the remaining body

bools.name: plnOuterKilledReturnPmp
bools.comment: returning instantly to the Prime Material if the Outer Plane body is killed

bools.name: plnCordSnapUnoccupiedDies
bools.comment: if the silver cord is snapped on the Astral Plane, the unoccupied body dies

bools.name: plnSubNoClassLimits
bools.comment: no limits to the number of characters of one class apply

bools.name: plnSubAlwaysCleric
bools.comment: there will always be 1 cleric

bools.name: plnSubMinMagicUser
bools.comment: if there are 2 or more in the party, there will also be a minimum of 1 magic-user

bools.name: plnSubBardFootnote
bools.comment: the BARD line carries the footnote: 7th or 8th level fighter ability, 6th to 9th level (d4+5) thief ability (the printed BARDT and 91h cells are the footnote-glyph and 9th garbles)
